html:
A carved ivory panel from Constantinople, made in the first half of the 6th century and now in the Louvre in Paris. It shows an emperor in triumph and is usually taken to be Justinian, though Anastasius I or Zeno have also been proposed.

The panel was made of five pieces; four survive. In the middle the emperor rides a rearing horse, spear in hand, while a figure of Victory crowns him and a defeated barbarian clings to the spear. Above, angels hold up a bust of Christ blessing. Below, foreign peoples bring tribute, including an elephant and a lion. Christ above the emperor is an early statement of Christian empire.

On the back is a list of Frankish kings and relatives of the queen Brunhilda, so it was in the Frankish kingdoms by the late 6th century. It takes its name from Cardinal Francesco Barberini, who owned it in the 17th century.
